title: How Language Models Organize Task Information
abstract: arXiv:2610.27724v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Dense linear probes assess task readability from language model (LM) representations, but do not directly reveal how many features suffice for prediction. We measure readout sparsity with \(k^*\), the smallest feature count found by a fixed search protocol that recovers 95% of dense-probe AUROC above chance. We evaluate 19 LMs from five labs on 14 core tasks. Ten base models give the nine reliably readable tasks similar feature counts and nearly the same order. This agreement extends to the selected features themselves, which on three tasks show cross-model response correspondence beyond class-mean differences and a label-correlation-matched null. Instruction-tuned deployment selectively reduces \(k^*\), with both weights and input format contributing. In controlled synthetic experiments across 20 models, successfully learned targets admit single-feature readouts, whereas readable controls require tens of features. Reference-model \(k^*\

translated_title: 语言模型如何组织任务信息
translated_abstract: 密集线性探针可以从语言模型（LM）的表示中评估任务的可读性，但无法直接揭示需要多少个特征才足以完成预测。我们用 \(k^*\) 来度量读出稀疏性——\(k^*\) 是通过固定搜索协议找到的最小特征数量，该协议能恢复密集探针高于随机水平95%的AUROC。我们在14个核心任务上评估了来自五个实验室的19个语言模型。十个基础模型在九个可靠可读的任务上给出相似的特征数量和几乎相同的排序。这种一致性延伸到所选择的特征本身——在三个任务上，这些特征展现出超越类均值差异、并超过标签相关性匹配零假设的跨模型响应对应性。指令微调会选择性地降低 \(k^*\)，其中模型权重和输入格式都有贡献。在跨20个模型的受控合成实验中，成功学习的目标仅需单特征读出即可，而可读的对照目标则需要数十个特征。
tldr: 该论文提出用最小稀疏特征数 \(k^*\) 来量化语言模型中任务信息的组织方式，发现不同基础模型在可读任务上使用相似数量的特征且所选特征跨模型存在对应关系，而指令微调会选择性地降低完成任务所需的特征数量。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces \(k^*\)—the minimal number of features needed to recover 95% of dense-probe AUROC—to quantify how language models organize task information, finding that diverse base models use similar feature counts with cross-model feature correspondence on readable tasks, while instruction tuning selectively reduces the required feature count.
